caption: 30° feels like 20°. Funny how we trust a weather app when it says a number doesn’t tell the whole story, but we let age define what we’re capable of. I’m 30. Swipe>>>> Age doesn’t define me. My lifestyle does. The girl in the old photos thought the answer was eating less, doing endless cardio, and chasing a smaller body. She believed confidence would come when she looked “perfect.” The woman in the first and the last photos knows better. I’ve been through crash diets, food guilt, and trying every shortcut. Today, I fuel my body, lift with purpose, rest without guilt, and eat enough to support the life I want to live, not just the body I want to see. Do I still have a little belly pooch? Yes. A little softness? Absolutely. But I also have strength, energy, confidence, and a relationship with my body that’s built on respect instead of punishment. At 30, I feel stronger, prettier, sexier, and more confident than I ever did in my twenties. And the best part? I know I’m only getting started. Your age isn’t what’s holding you back. Your daily habits are shaping the person you’ll become. So stop obsessing over the number. Start investing in your lifestyle. If you’ve ever struggled with crash dieting, body image, or not knowing where to begin, you’re in the right place. I’ll be sharing realistic nutrition, sustainable fitness, mindset shifts, and everything that helped me build a body I don’t need to fight anymore. Here’s to becoming the strongest, healthiest, and most confident version of ourselves. 🤍

I still remember my 29th birthday. Instead of simply celebrating, I spent the entire year putting pressure on myself because I thought it was my last year in my twenties. Society had convinced me that turning 30 meant I was running out of time—that somehow life, beauty, opportunities, and excitement had an expiry date. Then… I turned 30. And nothing changed. Except my perspective. I realized we’ve been sold the wrong story. Turning 30 isn’t the end of anything - it’s the beginning of becoming more comfortable in your own skin. Age is just a number. It doesn’t decide how much life you have left, it only tells you how many years you’ve lived. Some people don’t get the privilege of reaching 30, while others live to be 100. So why spend our precious time fearing a number? What truly matters is the quality of the life you’re creating. Are you choosing yourself every day? Are you becoming a better version of yourself than you were yesterday? Are you taking care of your body, your mind, and your soul? Is your heart still curious enough to explore, dream, and grow? If the answer is yes, then trust me… you’re just getting started. 🤍 P.S. One year later… and a piece of my heart is still somewhere in Europe. 🤍✨ A year ago, I packed my backpack and boarded a flight to Europe—all by myself. Looking back, I still can’t believe I actually did it. That trip gave me something I didn’t even know I was looking for: freedom with no tags. For the first time, I wasn’t thinking about who was watching me, what people would say, or whether I was doing things “the right way.” It was just me, unfamiliar streets, breathtaking views, kind strangers, and countless moments that quietly changed me forever. That solo backpacking trip wasn’t just another vacation—it was proof that dreams I once thought were “too big” could actually become reality. These photos could never capture everything I felt, but they’ll always remind me of the happiest, bravest version of myself. I don’t know when I’ll be back, but I know this isn’t goodbye. Europe, you’ve left a mark on my soul, and I can’t wait until we meet again. Hopefully, next year. 🌍❤️ Until then… here’s 60 memories in 6 seconds. We grew up romanticizing freedom through cinema. Imtiaz Ali’s women made it look effortless—to exist, to choose, to wander, to speak. But outside the frame, we are still gathering at Jantar Mantar to ask for rights that were never supposed to be a privilege. It’s unsettling and makes me wonder how much of the freedom we celebrate is lived, and how much of it only survives in books, films, and the Constitution. It’s strange that scenes which would feel heartbreaking in a movie are unfolding in real life. Maybe that’s the biggest plot twist of all, the freedom we romanticize on screen is still something we are fighting for off screen. #protest #freedom #cjpprotest #studentrights #democracy

I was hesitant to share this, and I still am. It feels like those “what’s on your mind?” kinda posts from Facebook back in the day (IFYKYK). It’s rare for my Instagram to have something so real, sad, and which is not just another reel. This isn’t a breakup story, just a girl trying to find true love in this f*cked up dating scenario, especially in a place like Delhi. Sometimes, I wonder if it’s bravery or just sheer foolishness to put yourself out there, to let someone else hold that much power over you, hoping they won’t crush it, and to be vulnerable, only to end up going nowhere. I feel exhausted and am losing hope to find the kind of love I desire (and deserve.) The best part is that—I know, no matter how dark it feels right now, I will be okay and reach a neutral place because I am the BIG girl from a small town, living in a big city, and who knows how to take care of herself. However, sadly, I don’t always wish to be that strong independent woman who faces life head-on, guides herself out of emotional turmoil, heals, and then finds the courage to do it all over again. But, I NEED to because I refuse to settle for the bare minimum. So, the bigger question is, will this be worth it? Absolutely! If this brings me the kind of care and love that feels safe, valued, respected, desired, and fosters growth and satisfaction. But, the mind plays games, and the question arises yet again, “What if it doesn’t?” And I ask myself, “Are you that person, who gives up so easily?” The answer is a resounding, NO. So, I gather myself, piece by piece, day by day. Even if today feels impossible, I may take as small a step as going to the gym, lifting some weights, and letting my heart out while stretching my sore body after an intense workout session.
Building, Rebuilding and growing. You always stand back up.
